readerTitle: Three small steps that add up to a third more sales
caseNote: 가상 사례 (푸드트럭, 사진 편집 앱) · 모든 수치는 설명용
insight: 제품을 파는 사업의 매출은 '고객 수 × 한 사람이 사는 횟수 × 가격'이며, 세 개의 작은 개선은 더해지지 않고 곱해진다.
misconception: 매출을 늘리려면 새 고객을 많이 데려오거나 가격을 크게 올려야 한다.

sources.text: 매출 분해의 표준 개념 (고객 수 × 구매 빈도 × 객단가)

factChecks.note: 선택지 계산을 확인하세요. 가격만으로 33%를 늘리려면 $10 × 1.33 = $13.30. 고객 수만으로 늘리려면 200 × 0.33 ≈ 67명 추가(기존 고객 3명당 1명).
사진 앱 계산을 확인하세요. 가격을 $40에서 $20으로 내리면 같은 매출에 판매량 2배가 필요합니다. 추가 팩은 기존 사용자 5,000명 중 5명에 1명(1,000명)이 $10에 사면 $10,000입니다.

cards.title: Three small steps that add up to a third more sales
body: A food truck sells a $10 lunch. Every customer pays, eats and walks away. Tomorrow, the till starts at zero again.
That is how most businesses in the world make money. And the way its numbers grow surprises many owners.

image.label: Food truck with a lunch line and an empty till
image.brief: 3D 클레이 스타일. 점심시간 푸드트럭 앞에 손님 줄이 서 있고, 트럭 옆에 "$0"이 표시된 빈 금전함과 아침 해가 보임. 실제 브랜드 로고나 상표는 쓰지 않음.

cards.title: You want about a third more revenue.
body: Your truck has about 200 regular customers. Each buys lunch about 3 times a month at $10. That's $6,000 a month.
You want to reach about $8,000. Which plan looks most realistic?

options.text: Raise the price by a third, to about $13.30
options.feedback: One quick move, but one lever carries the whole load. A jump that big gets noticed, and if regulars come less often, you lose part of the gain.
It works on paper. But you'd need one new regular for every three you have, which is a big marketing job for one truck.

options.text: Grow each a little: 10% more customers, 10% more visits, 10% higher price
options.feedback: Each step is small enough to manage. Together they multiply to about 33% more revenue. Next card shows the math.

cards.title: Follow one month of lunches.
body: Now add 10% to each: 220 × 3.3 × $11 = **$7,986**. Three 10% steps gave you 33% more, not 30%, because each step multiplies the others.

cards.title: Selling products
body: **Selling products** is the simplest way to make money. A customer pays once and owns the thing. You earn only when a sale happens.
So revenue is a formula with three levers: **how many customers**, how often each one buys, and the price. Most owners watch one lever. The formula says to work all three.

image.label: Three dials labeled customers, visits and price feeding one revenue meter
image.brief: 인포그래픽. "Customers", "How often they buy", "Price" 세 개의 다이얼이 곱하기 기호로 연결되어 가운데 "Revenue" 계기판으로 이어짐. 각 다이얼이 조금씩만 돌아가 있고 계기판은 크게 올라간 모습.

cards.title: Paid up front, earned again tomorrow.
body: This model has real strengths. Cash arrives at the moment of sale. Each sale has a clear cost and a clear amount left over, so it's easy to tell what's working.

The cost is that nothing carries over. A sale last month doesn't pay you this month. Each customer has to choose you again, every time. That's why **how often people buy** is often the lever with the most room to grow.

cards.title: Some products are bought daily, some once a decade.
body: A café's regulars may buy every morning. A sofa store's customers may come back in ten years.

When people buy often, small gains in visits add up fast. When people buy rarely, the levers shift: win new customers through referrals, and raise the value of each sale with add-ons, delivery or care plans.
The formula stays the same. Only the lever you lean on changes.

image.label: A coffee cup bought daily next to a sofa bought once a decade
image.brief: 좌우 분할 일러스트. 왼쪽은 커피잔과 매일 체크된 달력, 오른쪽은 소파와 10년 단위 타임라인에 점 하나. 실제 브랜드 로고는 쓰지 않음.

cards.title: The levers pull on each other.
body: The levers aren't independent. Raise the price and some customers may visit less. Offer a discount to bring them back more often and each sale leaves less money.
The multiplying works in both directions. If customers fall 10% and visits fall 10%, revenue drops about 19%, not 10%. Change one lever at a time, and check what the others do.

cards.title: Now it's a photo-editing app.
body: You sell a desktop photo app for $40, paid once. About 5,000 people own it and most still use it. New sales have slowed.

options.text: Cut the price to $20 to win more new buyers
options.feedback: You'd need twice as many sales just to earn the same. It also pushes on only one lever.

options.text: Sell an optional $10 pack of new filters to existing owners
options.feedback: It uses the buy-again lever on people who already trust you. If one in five owners bought it, that's $10,000. It must be worth paying for, or it will annoy them.

options.text: Put the whole budget into ads for new users
options.feedback: New users matter, and each one must be won from scratch. It ignores 5,000 owners who could buy again.

cards.title: Revenue is customers × how often they buy × price.
body: When you sell products, you're paid once per sale. Small gains on all three levers multiply into big ones.
**Try it today:** write down your three numbers for last month. Which lever have you never really tried to move?
